title: Minton's Playhouse sessions and keeping up with the new chords
summary: He often went to Minton's where Monk, Clarke and Dizzy worked out bebop; Crouch describes cutting sessions, and Stewart says his ear saved him.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Now did you ever go to any of the sessions that they were having at Minton's at that time?
Yes, quite a few times.
And you --
Minton's Playhouse.
Minton's Playhouse? That was when Monk -- I think Monk and Kenny Clarke had the house band.
That's right, yeah. I remember slightly.
And Dizzy.
Dizzy.
And a lot of the guys used to come through there.
Oh, yes.
Because that was when they were putting
the -- when they were trying to figure out how to make the bebop style work.
That's right, yeah.
Because -- did you ever play with Christian in that situation?
No, I don't think so, no.
Do you remember some of the guys who came through Minton's at that time?
Well, one was my old partner, Slim Gaillard was one of them.
Uh-huh.

And -- oh, gee. Let's see. It's hard for me right now to exactly remember. But all those whom from time to time who we have mentioned passed through Minton's Playhouse. Those were some good, beautiful sessions.

You know, it's said that -- Milt Hinton was saying that in Dizzy Gillespie's book, autobiography of memoirs, kind of -- it's going to come out sometime this year -- that Dizzy used to take him up on the roof of Minton's and give him his alternate sets of changes so they could run -- so the guys that couldn't really play, they could get rid of them.
I understand, yeah, cutting sessions and what have you.
Because it was like when they were
trying to play, they didn't want people --
I understand.
-- you know, sometimes (inaudible) guys would sit in who could only be playing one key.
There you go.
So (inaudible) modulate (inaudible) on them monk and them would a couple of times (inaudible).
Yeah, right.
So like when you played with them, you didn't have any problem with the styles - the chords that they were playing?
No problem whatsoever. Well, I'm very thankful that I had a very good ear, you know. I could hear what was happening. So that saved me, you know.
